subject: Nariway Signals - 2026-09-11 - Daskalopoulos gives away another 51 works and declines the tax deduction
html:
Nariway Signals
Friday, September 11, 2026
Lead
Dimitris Daskalopoulos gave away another 51 works to four more museums — and told them not to bother with his tax deduction
The National Gallery of Greece (29 works, the lion's share), MOMus in Thessaloniki, the Museum of Contemporary Art of Crete, and National Galleries of Scotland (3 works, including a Mike Kelley and a Bruce Nauman) are the new recipients; his representatives stated plainly he will not seek a tax benefit in any jurisdiction for the gift. It's a second act to a case this brief already tracks: his 2022 giveaway sent 350-plus works to EMST, Tate, and a jointly-owned Guggenheim/MCA Chicago grouping, on the same stated philosophy — "artworks do not belong to their owners." A living collector doing this twice, and saying out loud that the deduction isn't the point, is the sharpest available counter-example to every donor-intent and tax-motive story this brief otherwise tracks.
The Art Newspaper · Tate · Greek City Times
What's happening
A jewellery-fortune heir just gave a tiny Orkney museum its biggest gift since 1979 — a deliberate bet against London
Charles Asprey donated 53 contemporary works (Wolfgang Tillmans, Martin Puryear, Atelier E.B) to the Pier Arts Centre in Stromness, built on Margaret Gardiner's Modern British collection, plus funding for an artist residency and an acquisition budget. Explicitly framed as decentralizing collector philanthropy away from saturated capital-city institutions toward a small, specific place.
The Art Newspaper
The Rubell Museum's DC location relaunched this week, with a third Rubell generation reportedly now stepping into the collection
Don and Mera Rubell started collecting in 1964; son Jason and his wife Michelle have been full partners since 1982; grandchildren are now said to be involved too. A concrete public example of a major private collection handed down across generations while staying alive and still-growing, rather than freezing into a static bequest.
Miami Niche · Rubell Museum DC
Law & estates
The Wildenstein estate settled a $17M dispute with the IRS over where art is legally "situated" at death — down from a $98.1M assessment
The question was whether roughly 258 artworks Daniel Wildenstein shipped to a Swiss duty-free warehouse before he died, via a Bahamas-based trust, counted as part of his US taxable estate at all. Directly on-point for any T&E practitioner structuring offshore art storage or trust arrangements around a collection.
WealthManagement.com · ARTnews
A court upheld a 50%-of-income penalty against an art advisor for promoting an abusive art-donation tax shelter
The IRC §6700 penalty followed false statements about when ownership of donated art began and whether clients could rely on the advisor's own appraised values — a warning shot at advisors and appraisers, not just collector-donors.
WealthManagement.com · Tax Notes
Worth reading
Katya Kazakina, "Less Is More: Inside the Art World's New Season of Recalibration" (Artnet, Sept 9)
Fall is arriving leaner on purpose — galleries cutting fairs and rosters, collectors narrowing focus, "grow or go" dead — alongside real generational turnover among both collectors and artists.
Artnet
Tim Schneider, "The Great Wealth Transfer Is Art's Reddest Herring" (The Gray Market)
The contrarian case against the premise much of this brief's own coverage rests on: most of the trillion-dollar transfer won't be liquid or hit the open market, and mainly enriches the top tier of dealers, houses and advisors. Genuinely worth reading against, not merely alongside, this brief's own numbers.
The Gray Market
Greg Rook, "A Collector's Note — September" (Blackbird Rook, Sept 2)
First look at this newly-tracked advisor voice: a ground-level, object-by-object dispatch on three recent studio and collection finds — ballast against the market- and institution-level stories that dominate most of this brief.
Blackbird Rook
For the record
Single-owner collections made up 32% of Sotheby's/Christie's/Phillips fine-art sales value in H1 2026, per ArtTactic
The Art Newspaper reports the wealth-transfer wave is now visibly concentrated in the Impressionist/Modern market as older collectors downsize — the clearest market-level number yet for the pattern behind every estate-sale item this brief tracks individually.
The Art Newspaper
A restitution wrinkle surfaces in this week's Renoir Museum theft
Three of the four paintings taken from the Cagnes-sur-Mer house-museum on Sept 8 are "MNR" works — recovered after WWII but never claimed — and heirs of Jewish dealer Jadwiga Zak, who died at Auschwitz, have a pending restitution claim on one of the two still-missing paintings. Even an unclaimed, decades-settled collection can carry live provenance risk.
ARTnews · The Art Newspaper
To see — escalating
Christie's Alan Medaugh Hiroshige preview opens today — day one of one week. Public preview Sept 11–14, sale Sept 15, 20 Rockefeller Plaza; already on Alina's calendar for the Sept 12 preview.
ARTnews
New: Sotheby's single-owner Chinese-art preview also opens today. "Ritual, Cosmos, and Imperial Splendor" — 65 works, archaic bronzes to Buddhist sculpture and jades — previews Sept 11–16, sale Sept 17, Sotheby's New York. A second single-owner Asian-art preview opening the same morning as Hiroshige, two doors apart in Midtown.
Asia Week NY
The Bartos Mondrian's Paris leg closes tomorrow; the free New York leg is now 6 days out. Public-view legs: Paris Sept 9–12, New York Sept 17–20, Hong Kong Sept 25–29, London from Oct 8, sale Oct 14.
ARTnews
The Rothschild collection preview at Artcurial (Le goût Rothschild en héritage) is now 6 days out. Public preview Sept 17–22, sale Sept 22, Paris.
Artcurial
Sotheby's Open House (Sept 20–21, Sotheby's NYC HQ) is now 9 days out. Its confirmed program includes a session on legal considerations across an art collection's lifecycle, staged by the house's own trusts-and-estates practice.
Sotheby's
New: Sotheby's is mounting a selling exhibition from the Estate of John Chamberlain, Sept 18–27, NYC. "The Energy of Form" puts 19 works from the sculptor's own personal collection on view, timed to his 2027 centennial. Note-only for now.
Sotheby's
Rooms to be in
Next up: EPC of Westchester County's Fall Networking Event
Sept 23, Freebird Kitchen & Bar, 5pm — 12 days out. Non-members explicitly welcome (~$85), the lowest-pressure first visit to any of the four target councils.
Forward pipeline
  • Sept 17 — Matrons Mixer (Hall Rockefeller/Less Than Half), New York — registered, now 6 days out
  • Sept 17–22 — Rothschild preview at Artcurial, Paris (see To see, fly-and-stay)
  • Sept 20–21 — Sotheby's Open House, NYC (see To see)
  • Sept 23 — two CE webinars registered, plus the Westchester event above the same evening — worth stacking
  • Sept 28 — new find: EPC of NYC Lunch & Learn, "Navigating the Proposed NYC Pied-à-Terre Tax" — 17 days out
  • Oct 1 — Center for Art Law, "Artist Corporations: A New Legal Framework for Creative Practice," NYC (hybrid) — registered
  • Oct 5 — EPC of New York City's "Making Sense of AI" evening (confirm venue/fee)
  • Oct 21 — EPC of Westchester's dinner meeting, White Plains
  • Nov 4 — AAA Art Law Day, Cardozo School of Law, NYC — registered, a 250+-attendee art-law room
  • Nov 9–11 — CPAL "Estate & Legacy Planning 101," NYC — registered
  • Nov 12 — EPC of Bergen County breakfast, Wyckoff, NJ
  • Nov 17 — EPC of NYC's "Art Financing as an Important Tool for Wealth & Estate Planning" — already registered, Alina's first confirmed room
